title: Both stories instruct whitelisting Kendu on the shared multi-token batch minter while the only two artefacts that could prove Kendu is not fee-on-transfer are respectively vacuous and undone — leaving a latent arm-switch where one routine registerStream would point the DEV-01 pooled-custody defect at the live USDC buffer
specText: Story 072 Concerns, lines 458-463: 'Kendu is a meme token and the streamer has no fee-on-transfer support. Kendu Inu (0xaa95f26e…, 18dp) has a renounced owner() (0x0), which is reassuring — no live tax switch — but NudgeStreamer and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken both assume transfer(x) delivers exactly x. **The dry run must transfer a non-zero Kendu amount through collectNudge and assert the received balance equals the sent amount** before this goes to broadcast. If Kendu taxes transfers, it must not be whitelisted.' Story 072 Preflight line 514, UNTICKED: 'Confirm Kendu is not fee-on-transfer by round-tripping a non-zero amount through collectNudge.' Story 072 line 469: 'I have planned registerStream for USDC only, and left phUSD/Kendu whitelisted-but-unregistered.' Story 073 line 496: MockKendu is 'a new 18-decimal mock ERC20 mirroring MockSCX (public mint, no IBurnable, **no transfer fee**)'. Story 073 Verification line 540, ticked: 'Seed a phUSD and a Kendu donation through collectNudge so all three reward slots are non-zero; assert the Kendu amount received equals the amount sent (no fee-on-transfer).'
faithfulnessRouting: F-04 — PRIMARY. Law-1 story-unsafe escalation routed to the spec-conformance report. MUST NOT be filed into the QA/gas bundle.
description: Story 072 (lines 292, 522) and story 073 (Change 2, line 503) both instruct `setNudgeTokenWhitelist(KENDU, true)` on the shared BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, while NudgeStreamer.collectNudge credits `s.buffer += amount` unmeasured against pooled per-token custody (the DEV-01 defect, NudgeStreamer.sol:149-150). Story 072 is aware and installs the correct guard at lines 458-463 — 'If Kendu taxes transfers, it must not be whitelisted ... The dry run must transfer a non-zero Kendu amount through collectNudge and assert the received balance equals the sent amount before this goes to broadcast' — but its implementing Preflight line 514 is UNTICKED, so the real-token round-trip has not been performed. The apparent local substitute, story 073's `_seedNudgeStream` (DeployMocks.s.sol:1645-1666), asserts `require(received == amount, "nudge seed token is fee-on-transfer: streamer received < sent")` at :1661 — but against MockKendu, which story 073 line 496 itself defines as having no transfer fee. It proves a mock is fee-free and is vacuous as evidence about the real Kendu Inu at 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18.
impact: No armed path in the configuration the stories specify: story 072 line 469 registers a stream for USDC only and leaves phUSD/Kendu whitelisted-but-unregistered, so collectNudge is never called on Kendu, no Kendu buffer exists, and pullPendingStream no-ops on it. The residual is a latent arm-switch. One later `registerStream(newBM, KENDU, DURATION)` — routine-looking, the ordinary way to enable a reward slot, with no fee-on-transfer probe at that admission point and no re-review implied — arms DEV-01's pooled-custody drain against the LIVE USDC buffer: a taxed Kendu donation over-credits its buffer relative to custody, the shortfall is settled out of the shared per-token balance, and because batchMint loops pullPendingStream over the entire getNudgeTokens() whitelist inside one transaction, the revert takes down minting for EVERY reward token including USDC. The operator's evidence points the wrong way: a green deploy:local displays an FoT assertion passing, which is positive reason not to run story 072's line 514.
attackPath: PRECONDITION (sanctioned, and currently SAFE): both stories instruct setNudgeTokenWhitelist(KENDU, true) on the shared BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, while story 072 line 469 plans registerStream for USDC ONLY and leaves phUSD/Kendu whitelisted-but-unregistered. With no Kendu stream registered and donors donating only USDC, collectNudge is never called on Kendu, no Kendu buffer exists, and pullPendingStream no-ops on the unregistered token. The configured end-state is genuinely inert, exactly as story 072 claims.

THE EVIDENCE GAP: the obligation to prove Kendu is not fee-on-transfer is undischarged by both artefacts that appear to discharge it. (a) Story 072's own guard, Preflight line 514, is UNTICKED — the real-token round-trip against 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18 has not been performed. (b) Story 073's probe DOES exist in code (DeployMocks.s.sol:1645-1666, _seedNudgeStream) and DOES assert `require(received == amount, "nudge seed token is fee-on-transfer: streamer received < sent")` at :1661 — but it runs against MockKendu, which story 073 line 496 itself DEFINES as having no transfer fee. It proves a mock is fee-free and is vacuous as evidence about the real token, while its assertion string reads as though the FoT guard had been exercised.

THE ARM SWITCH: one later `registerStream(newBM, KENDU, DURATION)` — a routine-looking owner call, the ordinary way to turn on a reward slot, with no FoT probe at that admission point — arms the token.

IF KENDU TAXES: a Kendu donation then credits s.buffer by the amount SENT while custody receives less (DEV-01, NudgeStreamer.sol:149-150), and because custody is pooled per token with a per-stream cap, the shortfall is settled out of the shared balance.
CONSEQUENCE: batchMint's single-transaction loop over getNudgeTokens() reverts, taking the LIVE USDC reward leg down with it — the leg that by then holds the only real buffer.
evidence: Story 072 lines 458-463 (guard stated), line 469 ('registerStream for USDC only ... left phUSD/Kendu whitelisted-but-unregistered'), line 514 UNTICKED ('- [ ] Confirm Kendu is not fee-on-transfer by round-tripping a non-zero amount through collectNudge'), line 105 (Kendu Inu 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18, 18dp, owner() == 0x0 renounced). Story 073 line 496 defines MockKendu with 'no transfer fee'; line 540 ticked. Code at 3fb4e34: DeployMocks.s.sol:1645-1666 _seedNudgeStream mints via MockKendu(token).mint(deployer, amount) at :1651 and asserts received == amount at :1661; NudgeStreamer.sol:149-150 performs safeTransferFrom then s.buffer += amount with no delta measurement. Impact mechanics are PoC-proven under DEV-01: workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol, 4/4 PASS, including case B (cross-pair drain and revert) and case D (the divergence vanishes at feeBps == 0, i.e. the probe passes vacuously by construction).
recommendation: BEFORE the story-072 broadcast, discharge line 514 for real: round-trip a non-zero amount of the actual Kendu token at 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18 through collectNudge on a mainnet fork and assert received == sent. Record the transcript in the story; story 073's MockKendu probe does not discharge it and should be annotated to say so, since its assertion message currently reads as a general FoT guard. Structurally, move the admission check on-chain: probe for fee-on-transfer inside `registerStream` (already owner-gated and the natural admission point) so arming a taxed token fails closed rather than depending on a checklist — this is the same fix DEV-01 recommends and it closes both. Until then, do NOT register a Kendu stream, and record the whitelist-without-stream state as a deliberate, documented configuration with the arming hazard spelled out beside it.

classification.c4Criterion: C4 QA/Low today - an operational hazard and unverified-admission gap with no armed path. Would become C4 Medium ('the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements') the moment a Kendu stream is registered without the real-token round-trip. See reopenTrigger.
classification.assetImpact: None today, and never theft in any state. If armed, the impact is DEV-01's, on the AVAILABILITY axis only: pair A's settlement consumes the pooled per-token balance backing pair B, and the under-backed pair's pullPendingStream reverts — and because BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint loops pullPendingStream over the whole getNudgeTokens() whitelist inside one transaction, a single tainted token bricks the mint path for EVERY reward token, including the live USDC leg. Consistent with this repo's standing rule, cross-pot consumption of externally-derived yield is misallocation between protocol-owned pots, never economic loss.

classification.likelihood: low today, and the two conjuncts are honestly weak. (1) Kendu must actually tax transfers — unverified, but story 072 records owner() renounced to 0x0, so there is no live tax switch and only an immutable hard-coded fee would qualify. (2) An owner must register a Kendu stream. Neither has happened. What keeps the likelihood above negligible is that the operator's belief-forming evidence is wrong in the reassuring direction: a green local run displays an FoT assertion passing.
classification.assumptions: (1) Non-malicious owner throughout — rated purely as a Law-3 footgun, never as a malicious-admin vector. (2) Kendu is whitelisted per both stories' explicit instruction. (3) Mainnet registers a stream for USDC only, as story 072 line 469 sanctions and as this classification accepts. (4) The DEV-01 defect (unmeasured receipt against pooled per-token custody) remains unfixed. (5) Fee-on-transfer is IN SCOPE for this family — phoenix-nft-staking story-022 s4.4 documents FoT explicitly, so the C4 weird-ERC20 known-invalid predicate does not fire.
classification.externalRequirements: A future owner-executed registerStream on Kendu, AND Kendu in fact taxing transfers. Both are external to the current change and neither has occurred.

severityRationale: LOW — held DOWN against the auditor's proposed potential-medium, and held UP against QA. The brief asked for an honest rating on a conditional hazard gated on a future owner action, and this is the reasoning in both directions. WHY NOT MEDIUM. Four reasons, the first two decisive. (1) THE SANCTIONED END-STATE IS GENUINELY INERT, not merely claimed to be. Story 072 line 469 plans registerStream for USDC only and leaves Kendu whitelisted-but-unregistered; with no Kendu stream, collectNudge is never invoked on Kendu, no Kendu buffer exists, and pullPendingStream no-ops on the unregistered token. The DEV-01 pooled-custody drain additionally requires two pairs sharing one token, and a token with zero registered streams shares nothing. There is no armed path in the configuration both stories actually specify — so there is no availability impact to rate, and C4 Medium requires one. (2) IT WOULD DOUBLE-COUNT DEV-01. The impact described here IS DEV-01's impact, already filed at Medium with a 4/4-passing PoC. FAITH-L1-001's distinct content is narrower and different in kind: the story-level instruction to whitelist Kendu, the undischarged verification obligation, and the latent arm-switch. Rating the same availability failure at Medium under a second ID inflates the report's Medium count without adding a second impact — the exact dilution this pipeline rejects. (3) THE ARMING STEP IS A DELIBERATE OWNER CONFIGURATION CALL. registerStream is owner-gated, single-purpose and reviewable; the brief's own instruction is not to inflate to Medium where that is so. (4) THE FIRST CONJUNCT IS PROBABLY FALSE AND IS CHEAPLY CHECKABLE. Story 072 records Kendu's owner() renounced to 0x0, so no live tax switch exists; only an immutable hard-coded fee would qualify, and one cast round-trip settles it. WHY NOT QA, which is the more tempting error here. (1) THE STORY IS THE PROXIMATE CAUSE, WHICH MAKES THIS LAW-1 OVER LAW-2. Both stories INSTRUCT admitting an unverified memecoin into a contract that assumes exact delivery. Law 1 is explicit that where a story's own intended behaviour would introduce an exploit condition, the unsafe story must be flagged rather than the faithful implementation blessed — so this is a story-unsafe escalation, not a configuration note, and it carries securityEscalation:true. (2) BOTH GUARDS ARE ILLUSORY, AND ONE IS ILLUSORY IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION. Story 072's real-token round-trip (line 514) is UNTICKED. Story 073's probe exists and asserts `require(received == amount, "nudge seed token is fee-on-transfer: streamer received < sent")` at DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 — but against MockKendu, which story 073 line 496 DEFINES as fee-free. It cannot fail. Under this repo's standing principle that falsely-exhaustive or self-certifying evidence RAISES severity, a probe that looks like a guard but cannot fail is worse than no probe: an operator who ran deploy:local has WATCHED an FoT assertion pass and has positive reason not to run line 514. That is what lifts this clear of QA. (3) THE ARM SWITCH IS A TEXTBOOK LAW-3 NON-OBVIOUS FOOTGUN. Apply the test — would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised? registerStream(newBM, KENDU, D) reads as 'turn on the Kendu reward slot'. Nothing at that admission point probes for FoT, and nothing warns that enabling a NEW slot could consume the backing of the EXISTING live USDC one and revert batchMint for every reward token. Surprise, therefore footgun, therefore in scope and classified by the impact it unlocks. NET: LOW severity, MEDIUM-GRADE PRIORITY. The severity reflects that nothing is armed; the priority reflects that the only thing standing between the current state and DEV-01-on-live-custody is one routine owner call whose safety no one has actually verified. A mandatory REOPEN-AS-MEDIUM trigger is attached (see reopenTrigger) so this cannot quietly expire — under Law 1 that is the visible channel, not a log. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: story 073's Review Status is ISSUES_FOUND with two open HIGH issues and story 072 is in `incomplete`, so both acceptance criteria are non-final and line 514 may yet be ticked with real evidence — which would close this finding outright. That is expressed as confidence and as a reopen/close trigger, NOT as severity inflation. Verified as of story 073 @ 840 lines, story 072 @ 550 lines, and code @ 3fb4e34.
severityAgreement: DISAGREE - held at LOW against the proposed potential-medium. Rated as a conditional, owner-armed hazard with a mandatory REOPEN-AS-MEDIUM trigger rather than inflated to Medium today.
classifierNotes: PROPOSED SEVERITY OVERRIDDEN, downward: potential-medium -> low. Recorded explicitly because a downgrade of a securityEscalation finding must be auditable. The override rests on the sanctioned end-state being genuinely inert (registerStream for USDC only, so no Kendu stream and therefore no pooled-custody sharing on that token) and on the impact being DEV-01's, already filed at Medium — not on any doubt that the hazard is real. The reopenTrigger is the compensating control and is mandatory. KEEP SEPARATE FROM DEV-01 — do not collapse. DEV-01 is the CONTRACT defect (collectNudge credits amount sent, not received, against pooled per-token custody) and its fix is a code change in NudgeStreamer. FAITH-L1-001 is the STORY-LEVEL admission decision plus an undischarged verification obligation, and its fix is operational: run the real-token round-trip, and gate admission at registerStream. Distinct root causes, distinct fixes, distinct owners — the standing repo rule is not to collapse distinct guards. DEV-01 is the impact carrier and is cross-linked as such. NOT A MALICIOUS-OWNER VECTOR. Rated purely as a Law-3 non-obvious footgun under an assumed non-malicious owner. No part of this finding depends on the owner acting against the protocol. STORY-073 REVIEW CONTEXT, for the record: the story's embedded Review Issue 1 (HIGH) found the phUSD/Kendu collectNudge seed absent entirely — 0 collectNudge transactions in 345. That was REMEDIATED at 3fb4e34 ('[story-073] Seed phUSD/Kendu nudge streams'), and _seedNudgeStream now exists with a real received==amount assertion. This finding therefore does NOT re-file Review Issue 1; it observes that the remediation, while genuine code, is vacuous as evidence about the real token and may be mistaken for discharging story 072's line-514 obligation.

reopenTrigger.condition: ANY of: (a) registerStream(<any batchMinter>, KENDU, *) is executed on mainnet — or on any chain holding a real USDC buffer — without a COMPLETED real-token round-trip against 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18; (b) any second (batchMinter, token) pair is registered on a token that already has a registered stream, which arms DEV-01's cross-pair drain irrespective of Kendu; (c) a donor other than the USDC donors begins pushing into the streamer.
reopenTrigger.onTrigger: This finding becomes a live Medium instance of DEV-01 against real custody. Re-rate immediately; do not wait for the next scheduled run.
reopenTrigger.blockingPreBroadcastAction: Tick story 072 Preflight line 514 against the REAL Kendu token at 0xaa95f26e30001251fb905d264aa7b00ee9df6c18, not against MockKendu. Story 073's _seedNudgeStream probe does NOT discharge it.
reopenTrigger.law: Law 1 — parked in a visible channel with its reason, not in a log.

dedup.dedupDisposition: KEPT — NOT merged with DEV-01 (collapse considered and rejected)
dedup.dedupRationale: Shares DEV-01's impact mechanics but not its root cause, fix or owner. DEV-01 = a contract accounting defect fixed by measuring the receipt in collectNudge. FAITH-L1-001 = a story-level instruction to admit an unverified token plus an undischarged verification obligation, fixed operationally by running the real-token round-trip and gating admission at registerStream. Collapsing would erase the story-unsafe (Law-1-over-Law-2) escalation and the reopen trigger, and would leave no owner-visible record that story 072's own guard is unticked.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
